_readme: Funded PhD programmes, doctoral fellowships and PhD positions from OFFICIAL sources only. Same rules as internships.json: never invent dates or amounts; statusOverride null|varies|unconfirmed|closed. PhD scholarships already in scholarships.json are shown automatically on the PhD page. Checked weekly — see AGENT.md.

programmes.title: Marie Skłodowska-Curie Doctoral Networks (MSCA-DN)
programmes.summary: EU-funded PhD positions in international research networks across Europe. Hundreds of projects recruit doctoral candidates of any nationality, advertised individually on EURAXESS.
programmes.location: Universities and research organisations across EU and associated countries
programmes.fields: All research fields
eligibility: Must not hold a doctoral degree at the date of recruitment.
Must enrol in a doctoral programme for the project.
Mobility rule: must not have lived or had your main activity in the recruiting country for more than 12 months in the 36 months before recruitment.
programmes.nationalities: Any nationality.
programmes.funding: Employment contract funded by the EU: living allowance and mobility allowance, plus family, long-term leave and special-needs allowances where applicable.
programmes.duration: Usually up to 36 months (up to 48 months for Joint Doctorates)

dates.deadlineNote: Each network advertises its own positions with its own deadline on EURAXESS (list updated daily).

procedure: Search the EURAXESS list of MSCA Doctoral Network vacancies.
Check the mobility rule for the country of the recruiting organisation.
Apply directly to the network following each vacancy’s instructions.

verification.notes: From the European Commission’s MSCA Doctoral Networks page.

programmes.title: ISTA PhD Program
programmes.provider: Institute of Science and Technology Austria (ISTA)
programmes.summary: A fully funded, interdisciplinary PhD programme near Vienna with seven research tracks; students with a bachelor’s or master’s degree can apply, and all start on 15 September.
programmes.fields: Biology, chemistry and materials, computer science, data science and scientific computing, mathematics, neuroscience, physics
eligibility: Bachelor’s or master’s degree in a related field (or completing one).
CV, statement of purpose, answers to three questions, transcripts and three referees.
programmes.nationalities: No nationality restriction stated.
programmes.funding: Fully funded PhD programme (amount not stated on the application page).
programmes.duration: Several years; all students start on 15 September

dates.deadlineNote: Deadline 8 January 2027, 3 p.m. CET; reference letters by 12 January 2027.

procedure: Create an account on the online application portal (open only during the application period).
Submit CV, statement of purpose, transcripts and three referee contacts by 8 January 2027.

verification.notes: From ISTA’s PhD application page and graduate school homepage.

programmes.title: “la Caixa” Doctoral INPhINIT Fellowships — Incoming
programmes.summary: 30 four-year doctoral fellowships for researchers of any nationality to do a STEM PhD at top research centres in Spain or Portugal.
programmes.location: Severo Ochoa / María de Maeztu centres and Carlos III institutes (Spain) or FCT “excellent” units (Portugal)
programmes.fields: STEM: technology, engineering, physics, chemistry, mathematics, health and life sciences
eligibility: No more than four years of research activity before the deadline; not yet started a doctorate.
Studies that allow enrolment in an official PhD programme in Spain/Portugal by recruitment.
Mobility: not resided or had main activity in Spain/Portugal for more than 12 months in the 3 years before the deadline.
Accepted English certificate.
programmes.nationalities: Any nationality.
programmes.funding: Covers labour costs (employment contract), research costs and doctoral tuition fees; amounts in the rules for participation.

dates.deadlineNote: Closes 12 January 2027, 2 p.m. Spanish time. Shortlist 9 April; interviews 27–29 April; results 13 May 2027.

procedure: Choose a host centre/position from the call’s list.
Apply through the “la Caixa” portal by 12 January 2027.
Shortlisted candidates are interviewed in April.

verification.notes: From the “la Caixa” Foundation call page (Incoming Call 2027).

programmes.title: OIST PhD Program
programmes.provider: Okinawa Institute of Science and Technology (OIST)
programmes.summary: A five-year, English-language interdisciplinary PhD in Okinawa with full financial support, open to graduates with a bachelor’s or master’s degree.
programmes.fields: Interdisciplinary science: physics, chemistry, biology, neuroscience, mathematics, computing, engineering, environmental and marine science
eligibility: Bachelor’s or master’s degree (or completing one before enrolment).
Transcripts, statement of purpose, CV, 2–5 recommendation letters, English score if applicable.
Participate in the Admissions Workshop (interviews).
programmes.nationalities: No nationality restriction stated.
programmes.funding: Financial support starting about 2.6 million JPY a year (taxable), rising to about 3.6 million JPY; support is designed to cover tuition and living costs; subsidised campus housing; conference travel budgeted separately. Application fee 5,000 JPY.

dates.deadlineNote: The deadline for the 2027 entry cycle was 15 November 2026 (interviews 18 January – 7 February 2027). Dates for the next cycle are not yet published.

procedure: Check faculty and research units and supervision availability.
Apply online at the OIST graduate school portal before the deadline.
Shortlisted applicants attend the Admissions Workshop.

verification.notes: From OIST’s Apply to PhD and Student Support pages.

programmes.title: EMBL International PhD Programme
programmes.summary: Funded PhD positions in molecular biology and related fields at EMBL’s six sites in Europe, recruited twice a year.
programmes.location: EMBL Heidelberg, Hamburg, Barcelona, Grenoble, Rome and EMBL-EBI (Hinxton, UK)
programmes.fields: Life sciences, bioinformatics, physics, chemistry, computer science, engineering
eligibility: A university degree that formally qualifies you to enter a PhD (or expected before starting).
At least two academic references sent from institutional email addresses.
programmes.nationalities: All nationalities welcome; priority to EMBL member-state applicants if equally qualified.
programmes.funding: Funded PhD positions; EMBL charges no fee at any stage.
programmes.duration: Start by October 2027 at the latest (Winter 2027 round)

dates.deadlineNote: The Winter 2027 round closed on 12 October 2026. The Summer 2027 recruitment will open towards the end of January 2027.

procedure: Create an account on EMBL’s online application portal.
Complete the online form (do not upload CVs or letters).
Online screening interviews, then in-person interviews at an EMBL site.

verification.notes: From EMBL’s International PhD Programme application page.

programmes.title: EPFL doctoral programs
programmes.summary: EPFL’s 22 doctoral programs recruit PhD students several times a year; each program has its own deadlines (for example Computer and Communication Sciences: 1 December and 15 April).
programmes.fields: Engineering, computer science, mathematics, physics, chemistry, life sciences, architecture, energy, robotics and more
eligibility: Usually a master’s degree; each program sets its own requirements — check the program page.
programmes.nationalities: Requirements are set per program.
programmes.funding: PhD students at EPFL are normally employed as doctoral assistants (salary not stated on the deadlines page).

dates.deadlineNote: Deadlines differ by program, e.g. EDIC and EDEE: 15 April / 1 December; EDMX, EDEY, EDRS: 15 April / 15 December; EDBB, EDNE: 31 March / 1 November.

procedure: Choose a doctoral program and read its admission page.
Apply online by that program’s deadline.

verification.notes: From EPFL’s overview of doctoral application deadlines.

programmes.title: GSSI PhD programmes (L’Aquila)
programmes.summary: Fully funded international PhD programmes in L’Aquila in astroparticle physics, computer science, mathematics and regional science, with a scholarship, accommodation and board.
programmes.fields: Astroparticle physics, computer science, mathematics in natural/social/life sciences, regional science and economic geography
eligibility: Requirements are in each official call (normally a master’s degree or equivalent by enrolment).
programmes.nationalities: International applicants welcome (calls in English).
programmes.funding: 2026/27 call: gross scholarship of €16,243 a year plus accommodation in GSSI facilities (or a substitute grant), board and other benefits.

dates.deadlineNote: The 2027/28 call is not yet published. In 2026, deadlines were 4 May – 5 June depending on the programme.

procedure: Read the official call on the GSSI applications site.
Apply exclusively through the online procedure.

verification.notes: From GSSI’s 2026/27 call as published; next call not yet announced.

programmes.title: IOCB Prague PhD projects
programmes.provider: Institute of Organic Chemistry and Biochemistry of the Czech Academy of Sciences
programmes.summary: Annual call for PhD projects in chemistry, biology and physics at IOCB Prague; students enrol at a partner university and are paid a university scholarship plus an IOCB salary.
programmes.fields: Chemistry, biology, physics (life-science oriented)
eligibility: MSc or equivalent in life sciences or a related field.
Enrol at the partner university named by the supervisor (e.g. Charles University, UCT Prague).
programmes.nationalities: No nationality restriction stated.
programmes.funding: University scholarship plus a salary from IOCB (amounts not stated).

dates.deadlineNote: The 2026 call closed on 3 March 2026 (interviews 19 March). The 2027 call is not yet published.

procedure: Choose up to 3 projects in the call.
Submit CV, cover letter and BSc/MSc transcripts through the online form.
Shortlisted applicants are interviewed in Prague; then enrol at the partner university.

verification.notes: From IOCB Prague’s PhD call page (2026 call).

programmes.title: Australian Government Research Training Program (RTP) — international students
programmes.provider: Australian Government, awarded by each university
programmes.summary: Government-funded scholarships, awarded by Australian universities, that cover tuition and pay a living stipend to international PhD students.
programmes.fields: All research fields
eligibility: International students commencing or enrolled in a higher degree by research at the awarding university.
Competitive; each university sets its own criteria and rounds.
programmes.nationalities: International students.
programmes.funding: Tuition fee offset plus a stipend set by each university (e.g. University of Sydney: A$44,293 a year at the 2027 rate; Monash: A$36,063 a year), relocation/thesis allowances and health cover at some universities.
programmes.duration: Up to the length of the PhD (set by each university)

dates.deadlineNote: Example: University of Sydney — 18 December 2026 for research periods 3–4 of 2027. Monash: international rounds close 31 March and later in the year.

procedure: Find a supervisor and apply for PhD admission at the university.
Apply for the RTP scholarship in that university’s round.

verification.notes: From the University of Sydney RTP international page and Study Australia (Australian Government).

programmes.title: UKRI-funded PhD studentships (UK)
programmes.provider: UK Research and Innovation, through UK universities
programmes.summary: Research-council-funded PhD studentships advertised by UK universities; up to 30% of each new cohort can be international students.
programmes.fields: All research fields
eligibility: Apply to the university advertising the studentship — there is no route to apply to UKRI directly.
International students can fill up to 30% of new places in a cohort.
programmes.nationalities: Home and international students (international capped at 30% of a cohort).
programmes.funding: Stipend and fees set by the university within UKRI’s terms (check each advert).

dates.deadlineNote: Each university advertises its studentships with its own deadline — many close between December and March for October starts.

procedure: Search studentship adverts (e.g. on jobs.ac.uk and university websites).
Check that the advert accepts international applicants.
Apply to the university as instructed.

verification.notes: From UKRI (EPSRC) guidance on studentships.

programmes.title: International Max Planck Research Schools (IMPRS)
programmes.summary: 68 structured, three-year doctoral programmes run by Max Planck Institutes with partner universities; about half of the doctoral students come from abroad.
programmes.location: Max Planck Institutes and partner universities across Germany
programmes.fields: Natural sciences, life sciences, computer science, mathematics, humanities and social sciences (depends on the school)
eligibility: Open to talented German and foreign graduates; admission is highly selective.
Each school sets its own requirements and deadlines (usually a master’s degree).
programmes.nationalities: German and international students (about half are from abroad).
programmes.funding: Set by each school (the Max Planck page does not state amounts) — check the school’s call.

dates.deadlineNote: Each IMPRS runs its own recruitment with its own deadline; choose a school and check its website or contact its coordinator.

procedure: Choose an IMPRS whose research focus fits you from the Max Planck list.
Read that school’s call and deadline, or contact its coordinator.
Apply through the school’s own application system.

verification.notes: From the Max Planck Society’s IMPRS page.

programmes.title: SISSA PhD programmes (Trieste)
programmes.provider: SISSA — International School for Advanced Studies
programmes.summary: Funded PhD fellowships in mathematics, physics and neuroscience at SISSA in Trieste, with around 70 fellowships a year and calls in English for international candidates.
programmes.fields: Mathematics, physics, astrophysics, data science, neuroscience, genomics
eligibility: Requirements are in each programme’s information sheet (normally a master’s degree or equivalent).
Non-EU candidates are welcome to apply.
programmes.nationalities: EU and non-EU candidates.
programmes.funding: PhD fellowships (SISSA, FSE+ or project-funded); amounts are in the official call.

dates.deadlineNote: The 2027/28 call is not yet published. For 2026/27, deadlines ran from 19 January to 13 March 2026 for most programmes, with second sessions in August for some.

procedure: Read the SISSA PhD admission call and the information sheet for your programme.
Apply online through the PICA application system before the programme’s deadline.

verification.notes: From SISSA’s 2026/27 PhD admission call page; next call not yet published.

programmes.title: Pasteur–Paris University International Doctoral Program (PPU)
programmes.summary: Three-year paid PhD contracts at the Institut Pasteur in Paris for international students with a master’s in science or medicine, with a welcome bonus, yearly trip home and housing help.
programmes.fields: Life sciences, biomedical research, microbiology, immunology, neuroscience, computational biology
eligibility: A master’s degree or equivalent in science, medicine or related fields.
Apply to up to 4 projects on the PPU platform.
programmes.nationalities: International students (see the programme FAQ for mobility rules).
programmes.funding: Three-year employment contract: €2,000 a month (including social benefits), €4,000 gross welcome bonus, one return trip home a year (up to €1,300 from outside Europe), €750 a year for conferences and first-year housing help.

dates.deadlineNote: The call for October 2027 entry ran 1 October – 16 November 2026 (interviews in February). The next call is expected from October 2027.

procedure: Create an account on ppu.pasteur.fr and view the projects.
Apply to up to 4 projects; in November choose one.
Lab pre-selection, committee review in December, interviews in early February.

verification.notes: From the Institut Pasteur PPU programme page.

warnings: You need a supervisor at a Flemish university before applying.
programmes.title: FWO PhD Fellowship Fundamental Research (Flanders, Belgium)
programmes.summary: Four-year PhD fellowships at Flemish universities (KU Leuven, Ghent, Antwerp, VUB, Hasselt) for recent master’s graduates, applied for together with a supervisor.
programmes.location: Universities of the Flemish Community, Belgium
programmes.fields: All fields of fundamental research
eligibility: Affiliated to a Flemish university with a promotor (supervisor) willing to guide you.
A master’s-level degree at the start; no more than two years between your master’s and 1 March 2027.
Not previously funded by this fellowship; maximum two applications.
programmes.nationalities: No nationality requirement in the regulations (non-EEA diplomas need university confirmation of PhD access).
programmes.funding: Net monthly grant of at least €2,600 (indexed, linked to Flemish university assistant salaries), plus holiday pay and end-of-year bonus.

dates.deadlineNote: Opens 3 December 2026; closes 1 March 2027 at 5 p.m. CET. Applications are written and defended in English.

procedure: Find a promotor at a Flemish university and prepare the project together.
Submit through the FWO e-portal between 3 December 2026 and 1 March 2027.
Expert panels evaluate; the FWO Board of Trustees decides.

verification.notes: From FWO’s call page and fellowship regulations.

programmes.title: University of Auckland Doctoral Scholarship
programmes.summary: Tax-free stipend and tuition for doctoral students at New Zealand’s largest university; international applicants are considered automatically when they apply for a PhD place.
programmes.fields: All fields
eligibility: Apply for a doctoral place and tick that you want to be considered for scholarships.
Fees are covered for international students eligible to study under the domestic fees policy.
programmes.nationalities: Domestic and eligible international students.
programmes.funding: Tax-free stipend up to NZ$35,468 a year (2026 figure, adjusted yearly) for up to 42 months, tuition fees for eligible students, and student health insurance.

dates.deadlineNote: Apply for the doctoral programme by 1 November, 1 February, 1 May or 1 August to be considered in that round.

procedure: Find a supervisor and apply for a PhD place at the University of Auckland.
Indicate in the application that you want to be considered for scholarships.

sources.label: University of Auckland — doctoral scholarships for international students

verification.notes: From the University of Auckland’s doctoral scholarships for international students page.

programmes.title: KAIST PhD admission with KAIST Scholarship
programmes.provider: Korea Advanced Institute of Science and Technology (KAIST)
programmes.summary: International applicants to KAIST’s master’s and PhD programmes can choose the KAIST Scholarship, which covers full tuition, health insurance and a monthly stipend — 94% of international students receive it.
programmes.fields: Science, engineering, computing, business and more (all departments except GDI-GTIP)
eligibility: International applicants to a KAIST graduate programme (MS–PhD or PhD).
Select the KAIST Scholarship as your financial resource in the application to be considered (including for the KGPS/KPS presidential scholarships).
programmes.nationalities: International applicants.
programmes.funding: Full tuition, national health insurance and a monthly stipend that depends on research involvement and college.

dates.deadlineNote: Fall 2027 applications 7 January – 5 February 2027. (Spring 2027 entry closed on 1 September 2026.)

procedure: Choose a department on KAIST’s international graduate admission site.
Apply online between 7 January and 5 February 2027 and select the KAIST Scholarship.

verification.notes: From KAIST’s international graduate admission timeline and scholarship pages.

programmes.title: University of Tartu doctoral studies (junior research fellow positions)
programmes.summary: Estonia’s largest university admits doctoral students mainly into state-funded junior research fellow positions — paid employment with health insurance — with no tuition fees, including for international students.
programmes.fields: All fields — sciences, technology, medicine, humanities, social sciences
eligibility: A master’s degree or equivalent (may be checked by ENIC/NARIC).
English language requirements.
You can apply for one study place only per intake.
programmes.nationalities: International applicants welcome; no tuition fees for doctoral students, including international students.
programmes.funding: Most places are state-funded junior research fellow positions (salaried employment with national health insurance and paid leave). Full-time doctoral students also receive a doctoral allowance of €660 a month; excellent students can get a €400 a month performance stipend.

dates.deadlineNote: 1–15 February (selected specialisations; details by 15 January), 1–15 May (main intake; details by 20 April), 15–30 September and 15–30 November (selected specialisations). Check the open-calls page for the positions in each intake.

procedure: Check the open calls page for positions and topics in the current intake.
Apply online via DreamApply with all documents uploaded by the deadline.
Shortlisted candidates are interviewed.

sources.label: University of Tartu — status and funding of doctoral students

verification.notes: From the University of Tartu admission, open-calls and doctoral funding pages.

programmes.title: TalTech Early Stage Researcher PhD positions
programmes.summary: Four-year salaried PhD positions at Estonia’s technical university in Tallinn, advertised as competitions throughout the year, with no tuition fees.
programmes.fields: Engineering, IT, natural sciences, economics and business
eligibility: Master’s degree or equivalent; ranked on academic ability, achievements, motivation and an interview with the supervisor.
Upload all required documents (CV, ID, qualifications) — incomplete applications are rejected.
programmes.nationalities: International applicants welcome (application fee €100 from 1 June 2026, with exemptions such as EU citizens and Estonian graduates).
programmes.funding: Employed as an Early Stage Researcher with a salary guaranteed for 4 years — at least the average monthly salary in Estonia (minimum €2,300 gross full time in 2025). No tuition fees.

dates.deadlineNote: Early Stage Researcher competitions are announced throughout the year, each with its own deadline.

procedure: Browse open competitions on the TalTech application portal and choose a topic.
Upload all documents and pay the fee if required.
Submit before that competition’s deadline; interview with the supervisor.

verification.notes: From TalTech’s PhD admission page.

programmes.title: Vilnius University doctoral studies
programmes.summary: Doctoral studies at Lithuania’s oldest university; full-time students in state-funded places receive a monthly stipend set by the Government of Lithuania.
programmes.fields: Sciences, medicine, humanities, social sciences (topics can be pursued in English)
eligibility: A master’s degree or equivalent (foreign qualifications assessed by the university).
Two recommendations from doctoral-degree holders and a research project.
Studies take place in person in Lithuania.
programmes.nationalities: Open to applicants with a recognised master’s degree; check eligibility for state-funded places in the admission rules.
programmes.funding: State-funded full-time places: €1,406 a month in year 1 and €1,628 a month from year 2 (2026 rates).

dates.deadlineNote: 2027 dates are not yet published. In the 2026 cycle, deadlines differed by field (e.g. Medicine 26 October; Economics and Political Sciences 15 December).

procedure: Read the admission rules for your field.
Apply through the VU admission system (ISAS) with recommendations and research project.

sources.label: Vilnius University — apply to doctoral studies

verification.notes: From Vilnius University’s doctoral admissions page.

programmes.title: Kaunas University of Technology (KTU) doctoral studies
programmes.summary: State-funded and self-funded doctoral places in technology, science and social sciences at KTU, with a monthly scholarship for state-funded students; the main admission is in June–July.
programmes.fields: Engineering, technology, natural and social sciences, architecture
eligibility: Recognised master’s degree; some third-country qualifications also need the OMPT-D mathematics test (75%+).
English B2 / IELTS 5.5 / TOEFL 75 (issued within 2 years).
Interview with the doctoral committee.
programmes.nationalities: International applicants welcome (application fee €132 for non-Lithuanian citizens).
programmes.funding: State-funded places: no tuition and €1,406 a month in year 1, €1,628 a month in years 2–4 (from 1 January 2026). Self-funded tuition €12,680 a year.

dates.deadlineNote: Admission is currently closed. KTU will publish the 2027 regulations in February 2027; the main admission runs in June–July.

procedure: Start the online application to get the fee invoice.
Upload diploma, CV, two recommendations (one from the supervisor), research proposal and English certificate as PDFs.
Attend the interview; sign the learning agreement if invited.

verification.notes: From KTU’s PhD admissions page.

programmes.title: University of Latvia doctoral studies
programmes.summary: Doctoral admission at Latvia’s largest university, with state-funded and self-funded places; international applicants living abroad apply online by an earlier deadline.
programmes.fields: Sciences, humanities, social sciences, medicine
eligibility: Master’s degree (legalised diplomas and transcripts with translations).
Doctoral research proposal (ideally with a prospective supervisor), CV and motivation letter.
English test if your previous degree was not taught in English.
programmes.nationalities: International applicants welcome; who can apply for state-funded places is explained on the university’s (Latvian-language) page.
programmes.funding: State-funded and self-funded places (amounts not stated on the English page). Registration fee €30 online or €40 in person.

dates.deadlineNote: 2027 dates are not yet published. In 2026, applicants living outside Latvia had to apply by 1 May (non-EU) or 31 May (EU/EEA/Swiss); general submission was 17–28 August.

procedure: Prepare your research proposal with a prospective supervisor.
Apply online via apply.lu.lv (if living abroad) with legalised documents.
Take the entrance examination in September.

verification.notes: From the University of Latvia Doctoral School admission page (2026).

programmes.title: Riga Technical University (RTU) doctoral studies
programmes.summary: Doctoral studies at Latvia’s technical university in Riga; international applicants apply online with a PhD study proposal and a scientific plan agreed with a supervisor.
programmes.fields: Engineering, IT, energy, materials, architecture, economics
eligibility: Master’s degree (evaluated by Latvia’s ENIC/NARIC centre — allow up to a month).
PhD study proposal, scientific plan and supervisor recommendation; video interview.
programmes.nationalities: International applicants welcome.
programmes.funding: Funding is not stated on the admission page — check individual RTU PhD calls (some institutes advertise funded positions). Application fee €150.

dates.deadlineNote: The admission page does not list deadlines; check apply.rtu.lv for the current intake.

procedure: Create an account on apply.rtu.lv and pay the €150 fee.
Submit a PhD study proposal; agree a scientific plan with your supervisor.
Complete the video interview.

verification.notes: From RTU’s doctoral admission page.

programmes.title: CRG International PhD Programme (Barcelona)
programmes.summary: Funded four-year PhD positions in genomics and biomedicine at a leading Barcelona research centre, open to candidates of any nationality.
programmes.fields: Genomics, systems biology, bioinformatics, cell and developmental biology, biomedicine
eligibility: Bachelor’s and master’s in biomedical sciences (minimum 300 ECTS) or an equivalent degree that allows starting a PhD in Spain.
Choose up to two CRG labs; two reference letters requested through the system.
programmes.nationalities: Any nationality.
programmes.funding: Four-year annual work contract with a competitive salary, full health and occupational insurance and Spanish social security.

dates.deadlineNote: Deadline 22 November 2026. Apply online only (no email applications).

procedure: Register on the CRG recruitment system and choose up to two labs.
Complete the online application before 22 November 2026.

verification.notes: From the CRG International PhD Programme 2027 call page.

programmes.title: Vienna BioCenter PhD Program
programmes.provider: Vienna BioCenter (IMP, IMBA, GMI, Max Perutz Labs)
programmes.summary: International PhD programme in molecular life sciences at the Vienna BioCenter; students are employed by their host institute, with calls in spring and autumn.
programmes.fields: Molecular biology, biochemistry, structural biology, neuroscience, plant biology, bioinformatics
eligibility: See the programme’s eligibility criteria page before applying (needs a u:account).
Written application, online panel interviews, then interviews with research groups.
programmes.nationalities: International applicants welcome; non-EU/EEA students pay a semester fee unless they obtain equal status (tuition fees are reimbursed).
programmes.funding: Employed by the host institute: €39,000–42,900 gross a year (2025), with health, pension, accident and unemployment insurance; tuition fees reimbursed.

dates.deadlineNote: Two calls a year: spring call opens 1 March, autumn call opens 1 September (autumn 2026 deadline was 15 October). The spring 2027 deadline is announced with the call.

procedure: Create a u:account and read the application instructions.
Submit the written application with two references in the call window.
Attend online panel and research-group interviews.

verification.notes: From the Vienna BioCenter PhD Program applications page.

programmes.title: Politecnico di Milano PhD calls (42nd cycle)
programmes.summary: Italy’s largest technical university recruits PhD candidates in several calls a year across engineering, architecture and design.
programmes.fields: Engineering, architecture, design, data science, management
eligibility: Requirements are in each call (normally a master’s degree or equivalent by enrolment).
programmes.nationalities: International applicants can apply (requirements in each call).
programmes.funding: Scholarships and positions are listed in each call (amounts not stated on the overview page).

dates.deadlineNote: 3rd call opens 14 December 2026, deadline 14 January 2027 (start 1 February 2027). 4th call: 15 March – 15 April 2027 (start 1 May 2027).

procedure: Read the call and the list of positions for your PhD programme.
Apply online by the call deadline.

sources.label: Politecnico di Milano — PhD calls and open positions

verification.notes: From Politecnico di Milano’s PhD calls and open positions page.

programmes.title: FNR PRIDE Doctoral Training Units (Luxembourg)
programmes.provider: Luxembourg National Research Fund (FNR), through host institutions
programmes.summary: Luxembourg’s main doctoral funding programme: FNR funds blocks of four-year PhD positions in Doctoral Training Units at the University of Luxembourg and the research institutes, and candidates apply directly to the units for advertised positions.
programmes.location: University of Luxembourg, LIST, LIH and LISER
programmes.fields: Varies by Doctoral Training Unit
eligibility: Apply directly to a funded Doctoral Training Unit for an advertised PhD position (project scope largely pre-defined).
Master’s degree (PhD candidate with a master’s).
programmes.nationalities: Open internationally — the FNR reports PRIDE positions are predominantly filled by international candidates.
programmes.funding: Each PhD grant covers the equivalent of a 4-year PhD employment contract plus a €6,500 training and mobility allowance.

dates.deadlineNote: Positions are advertised by each funded Doctoral Training Unit with its own deadline (see the University of Luxembourg and institute job pages).

procedure: Look for PRIDE / Doctoral Training Unit PhD positions on the University of Luxembourg, LIST, LIH and LISER job pages.
Apply to the unit as instructed in the advert.

sources.label: FNR — three routes to the PhD

verification.notes: From FNR’s PRIDE page and its 2025 overview of doctoral funding.

warnings: FNR’s individual PhD grant (AFR) has ended; its successor “doctoral training aid” requires 5+ years of education or residence in Luxembourg, so it is not listed here.

portals.label: EURAXESS — MSCA doctoral vacancies
portals.note: European Commission list of EU-funded positions, updated daily.

portals.label: EURAXESS — all research jobs
portals.note: Search “PhD” or filter First Stage Researcher (R1) for doctoral positions across Europe.

portals.label: PhDGermany (DAAD)
portals.note: DAAD database of open PhD positions aimed at international applicants.

portals.label: DAAD International Programmes — PhD
portals.note: DAAD guide and database of structured, international doctoral programmes.

portals.label: ADUM
portals.note: Network used by French doctoral schools to publish doctoral offers (mostly in French).

portals.label: AcademicTransfer — PhD jobs
portals.note: Job site of Dutch universities and research institutes; Dutch PhD candidates are usually salaried employees.
